conceptual assets.information: This is the system information returned to software, including the clock-frequency value and the configured memory, hart, boot, cache, debug, bus, and peripheral capabilities on which system discovery and configuration depend. The build-time fields have no entry port, while the clock-frequency field enters through bus_req_i.data; the information leaves through the bus response data field.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The information can expose security-relevant hardware configuration, including OCD enable and authentication status, through bus_rsp_o.data at line 168 from fields generated at lines 113 and 120. The clock-frequency portion can be overwritten directly from bus_req_i.data at line 95 when the unchecked write condition at line 94 is met. The response data is withheld or forced to zero when buf_ack is inactive at line 168, with buf_ack generated from the request strobe at line 160 and returned as the response acknowledge at line 169.
conceptual assets.attack: An unauthorized bus master could read the response to disclose the system security and capability configuration, write a false clock-frequency value through the unchecked bus write path, or disrupt the request/acknowledge transfer so the readback is unavailable.

considered, not kept.concept: Build-time generic settings as independent assets

considered, not kept.reason: The transaction is only used to select, transfer, and acknowledge the system-information access; forwarded bus transactions are not a conceptual asset of this unit.
buf_adr only copies the access address and indexes the readback while the access is served, so it is a held address rather than information of its own.
buf_ack only repeats the request strobe to time the bus response and is excluded as a bus-handshake copy.
clk_i and rstn_i only time or reset the internal storage and response path, and clocks and resets are excluded from conceptual assets.
